Utilization Permission: Industrial units, excluding garment industries, must obtain a Utilization Permission (UP) based on Utilization Declaration (UD) for bonded raw materials before starting production.
Garment industries involved in both direct and deemed exports are mandatory required to obtain a UP for their deemed export activities.
The application for a UP must be submitted to the designated Assistant or Deputy Commissioner at the relevant Customs Bond Commissionerate, Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate, or Custom House.
An approved UP requires a minimum value-addition rate of fifteen percent and must be uploaded to the relevant Commissionerate website with copies sent to associated stakeholders.

Bonded raw materials must be 'ex-bonded' from the warehouse for production only in accordance with the approved UP, and the UP itself is subject to strict conditions including the prohibition of importing restricted items and requirements for proper accounting of waste materials.
Assistant/Deputy/Joint Commissioner of C: The officer in charge of the UP section is responsible for verifying documents, including checking databases from the central bank and relevant industrial associations, before recommending the UP for approval.
The Assistant or Deputy Commissioner holds the authority to approve the Utilization Permission upon being satisfied with the submitted documents and recommendations.
Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority: For industries affiliated with this authority, an Import Permit (IP) serves as a functional substitute for the Utilization Declaration or Utilization Permission during the application process.
Commissioner of Customs (Bond): The Customs Bond Commissionerate serves as one of the designated offices where applications for the Utilization Permission must be submitted along with all required supporting documentation.
Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT: The relevant Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate acts as a primary office for receiving applications for Utilization Permission and overseeing the administrative process for the industries under its jurisdiction.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the issuing authority for the Utilization Permission, as outlined in the provided schedule form.

Export of Manufactured Goods: Manufactured goods produced using raw materials under an approved utilization permission must be exported through a designated customs house or customs station.

Export General Manifest: Following shipment, an export general manifest generated by the customs computerized system must be maintained by the exporting entity for audit purposes.
Bill of Export: A copy of the bill of export must be preserved alongside other export documentation to facilitate future customs audits.
Deemed Export: Deemed exporters must issue Value Added Tax invoices for supplied goods, ensuring that specific details such as utilization permission numbers, back-to-back letter of credit numbers, and direct exporter information are accurately recorded on the invoice.
Value Added Tax Invoice: All Value Added Tax invoices and supporting export documentation must be retained by the relevant entity for the purpose of subsequent audit inspections.
Export Proceeds Repatriation: Entities are required to provide proof of export proceeds repatriation, including copies of foreign demand drafts and proceeds realization certificates, during the course of an audit.

Bonded Warehouse: Industrial enterprises are permitted to hold a license to operate simultaneously as both direct and deemed exporters.
Existing warehouse license holders may apply to change their status to operate as both direct and deemed exporters with the approval of the licensing authority.

All imported or collected raw materials must be entered into the bonded warehouse under the supervision of a bond officer and recorded in the bond register upon usage against a utilization declaration.
Bonded Warehouse License: Applications for new licenses involving both direct and deemed exports require specific recommendations from the investment board and relevant associations.

To modify an existing license to include additional export categories, enterprises must obtain recommendations from relevant associations and approval from the investment board before applying to the licensing authority.
The license must be updated to include the details and HS codes of all materials and finished goods used in both direct and deemed export operations as recommended by the investment board.
Annual Import Entitlement: For industries other than garment manufacturing, the annual import entitlement is determined based on the production capacity of declared machinery and in accordance with the relevant rules and consumption coefficients approved by the department.
Utilization Declaration: Issuance of a utilization declaration is mandatory for both direct and deemed exports.
For deemed exports, a utilization declaration cannot be issued without the consumption coefficient approved by the department.
Direct Export Procedures: When importing materials for direct export based on export letters of credit, sales contracts, and utilization declarations, the materials must be recorded in the passbook and bond register.

Exporters must ensure the utilization of imported materials against the utilization declaration, record the usage in the bond register and passbook, and complete the ex-bonding process to finalize the export.

Warehouse Licensing Rules 2024: These rules establish the regulatory framework and timeframes for submitting annual audit documents for industrial warehouse licensees.
The rules govern the conduct of audits by customs authorities and specify the documentation and information that must be presented in audit reports.
Industrial Warehouse Licensee: Licensees must submit comprehensive annual import-export reports and supporting documentation to the relevant Customs Commissionerate one year after receiving their license.
Failure to submit audit documentation within the prescribed time limits subjects the licensee to legal action under existing laws and these rules.
Customs Commissionerate: The Commissionerate is responsible for receiving and reviewing audit documentation from warehouse licensees and conducting official audits within the defined timeframes.
The Commissionerate has the authority to issue sector-specific orders regarding the preparation of audit reports and the documentation required for such audits.
Audit Report: The audit report must contain detailed information on remaining raw materials, export orders, and utilized raw materials per the standard utilization permission.
The report must also include specific data on product supply, value repatriation, consumption patterns, wastage coefficients, and financial data related to energy and exports.
